title: Tumor Spheroid Fabrication and Encapsulation in Polyethylene Glycol Hydrogels for Studying Spheroid-Matrix Interactions
protocol: Scoop the elastomer into a weigh boat using a spatula and weigh it for negative PDMS precursor solution preparation.
Add curing agent to the elastomer base at a 1:10 ratio for negative PDMS precursor solution preparation.
Mix the PDMS and curing agent gently and thoroughly using the spatula in the plastic weigh boat for negative PDMS precursor solution preparation.
Scoop the elastomer base into the weigh boat using a spatula and weigh it for positive PDMS precursor solution preparation.
Add curing agent to the elastomer base at a 1:9 ratio for positive PDMS precursor solution preparation.
Mix the PDMS and curing agent gently and thoroughly using the spatula in the plastic weigh boat for positive PDMS precursor solution preparation.
Pipette 1 mL of TEA and 9 mL of 1x phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) to a 50 mL conical using a pipette aid to create a 0.75 M TEA solution.
Titrate the solution to a pH of 8 using 1 N HCl or 1 N NaOH.
Add enough 1x PBS to achieve a final volume of 25 mL to achieve a final TEA concentration of 0.3 M with a pH of 8.
Prepare complete media by adding 56 mL of fetal bovine serum and 5.6 mL of penicillin and streptomycin to 500 mL RPMI medium.
Place the prepared complete media at 37 °C for 10-20 min until warm.
Store the complete media at 0-4 °C for up to 6 months.
Weigh 20 mg of 4-arm PEG-Acrylate (4-arm PEG-Ac) powder in a microfuge tube.
Add 70 µL of 0.3 M TEA buffer to the powder.
Vortex the solution until fully dissolved.
Adjust the final volume to 100 µL by adding approximately 27 µL of TEA buffer.
Weigh 20 mg of PEG-diSH powder in a microfuge tube.
Add 70 µL of TEA buffer to the PEG-diSH powder.
Vortex the solution for about 30 seconds or until fully dissolved.
Adjust the final volume by adding enough TEA buffer (~27 µL) to reach a total of 100 µL.
Mix 20 µL of basement membrane matrix (LDEV-free) with 9.98 mL of complete media thoroughly.
Warm the mixture to 37°C and use immediately.
Mix 891 µL of 1x PBS and 108 µL of paraformaldehyde (37% w/v concentration).
Add 1 µL of nonionic surfactant (100% concentration) to the mixture.
Mix thoroughly to prepare cell fixative solution.
Prepare 3 mM of 3,3'-dihexyloxacarbocyanine iodide (DiOC) by mixing 2.65 mg of DiOC in 1 mL of DMSO.
Prepare 1.5 mM of propidium iodide solution (PI) by mixing 1 mg of PI in 1 mL of de-ionized water.
Prepare clearing solutions of 20%, 40%, and 80% v/v formamide in 1x PBS for spheroid clearing.
Mix 8 mL of 1x PBS with 2 mL of formamide to prepare 10 mL of 20% v/v formamide solution.
Mix 6 mL of 1x PBS with 4 mL of formamide to prepare 10 mL of 40% v/v formamide solution.
Mix 2 mL of 1x PBS with 8 mL of formamide to prepare 10 mL of 80% v/v formamide solution.
Vortex the mixed solutions for about 30 seconds.
Prepare 2 g (~1 mL) of negative PDMS precursor solution.
Pour the PDMS precursor solution onto one well of a 6-well square pyramidal master mold.
Degas the PDMS precursor solution by placing the 6-well square pyramidal plate in a vacuum desiccator for 30 minutes.
Cure the PDMS by placing the plate into a 60 °C oven for 24 hours.
Ensure the plate lid is removed for degassing and placed back on for curing.
Degas the solution in a vacuum desiccator or through purging with an inert gas such as nitrogen or argon.
Place the negative PDMS mold from the master mold using a spatula.
Cut the negative mold in a 35 mm diameter slab using a biopsy punch.
Remove negative molds using a spatula to get between the well plate and the PDMS mold.
Gently pull the negative mold from the master mold.
Place the 35 mm slabs of the negative PDMS mold into a 35 mm Petri dish with the textured microwells facing up.
Prepare 2.5 g of positive PDMS precursor solution and pour it onto the negative mold in a 35 mm Petri dish to cover completely.
Degas the precursor solution for 30 min.
Place the covered negative mold into a 60 °C oven for 3-4 h.
If a bubble forms under the negative mold, push the mold down gently using a spatula or continue degassing for an additional 30 min if bubbles remain.
Once the positive PDMS mold cures, remove it from the Petri dish and slightly cut into the positive mold to expose the interface with a razor.
Peel away the edges of the circular mold and gently peel the negative mold from the positive mold.
Cut the positive molds into slabs using a 10 mm biopsy punch.
Prepare the PDMS glue precursor solution (~0.5 mL or 1 g) as previously described.
Dip the flat side (not the side with the pattern of microwells) of the 10 mm positive mold into the PDMS precursor solution using tweezers.
Place one mold per well of a 48-well plate and gently press each mold to the well bottom using tweezers.
Place the assembled plate in a 60 °C oven for 4-24 h to allow the PDMS glue to cure.
Wipe off any PDMS glue precursor solution from the positive mold microwells if necessary, and repeat the gluing step.
Add 300 μL of 70% ethanol into each well of the 48-well plate using a 1000 μL pipette.
Aspirate the 70% ethanol and place the 48-well plate uncovered in a tissue culture hood under UV (302 nm) for 2 h.
Wash microwell molds with an anti-adherence rinsing solution by adding 300 µL to each well using a 1000 µL pipette.
Centrifuge at 1620 x g for 3 min and aspirate the solution using a vacuum pump and a Pasteur pipette.
Expose cells to ~80 µL of 0.25% trypsin/EDTA per each cm² of the culture flask area for 5 min at 37 °C.
Neutralize the trypsin by adding an equal volume of complete cell culture medium.
Collect the cells from the tissue culture flask.
Transfer 10 µL of the cell suspension into each port of a hemocytometer for cell counting.
Count the total number of cells and average that count from at least 8 quadrants, ensuring the cell number in each quadrant is 20-50.
Multiply the calculated number by 104 to determine the final cell concentration.
Resuspend the collected cells in complete RPMI cell culture medium supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum and 1% penicillin/streptomycin at a desired final cell concentration.
Place 500 μl of cell suspension in microwells.
Centrifuge the plate at 1620 x g for 3 min.
Incubate the plate in a humidified incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 24 h to allow spheroids to form.
Firmly pipette 500 μl of complete medium into the well.
Flush the four quadrants of the well with 500 μl of medium three to four times using a 1000 µL pipette to dislodge the spheroids.
Gently aspirate the medium containing the spheroids (~1000 μl total) into a microcentrifuge tube using a 1000 µL pipette.
Allow the spheroids to settle to the bottom of the microcentrifuge tube.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the spheroids to the desired final concentration.

Combine 50 µL of the spheroid suspension, followed by 30 µL of 20% w/v 4-arm PEG-Ac and finally 20 µL of 20% w/v PEG-diSH in a microcentrifuge tube to create 100 µL of a 10% w/v PEG hydrogel precursor solution.
Mix the gel precursor solution by pipetting up and down approximately 10 times.
Pipette 20 µL of the gel precursor solution between two parafilm-lined glass slides separated with 1 mm silicon spacers.
Place the slides with gel precursor solution in a 37 °C, 5% CO2 incubator for 15 min to allow for gelation.
Separate the two glass slides once hydrogel gelation is complete.
Gently peel the gels off the glass plate using a spatula.
Place the gels into a 24-well plate, one per well, ensuring the surface containing the spheroids faces up.
Invert the multiwell plate containing spheroids during gelation to ensure they are near the surface of the hydrogel for better access to nutrients and oxygen.
Monitor gelation by inverting the tube with the remaining hydrogel precursor solution until it stops flowing.
Add complete medium (~500 µL) to each well to completely submerge the hydrogel.
Place the multiwell plate in a humidified incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for cell culture.
Change the media every 2-3 days during cell culture.
Culture the hydrogels for up to 4 weeks or until they degrade, changing the media every other day as needed.
Use DiOC (3 mM) at a concentration of 0.02 µg/mL to determine cell viability by staining mitochondria and endoplasmic reticulum in cells.
Add 2 μL of DiOC per every 1000 μL of media into the flask culturing the dissociated cells, at least 24 h prior to forming spheroids.
Aspirate all media from the cells.
Rinse the gel by adding 500 μl of 1x PBS using a pipette, ensuring complete submersion of the gel.
Aspirate the PBS and add 500 μL of fresh media to each well.
Add 30 μL of PI solution (6 μL per every 100 μL of media) to each well.
Cover the well plate with aluminum foil to protect it from light.
Incubate the well plate at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 30 min.
Remove the foil and aspirate the media from the wells.
Rinse the gel by adding 500 μl of 1x PBS using a pipette, then aspirate it.
Repeat the rinse two additional times with fresh 1x PBS.
Add 500 μL of media to each well after rinsing.
Image under a fluorescent inverted or confocal microscope.
Aspirate the media from the wells containing hydrogels.
Rinse the hydrogels by adding 500 µl of 1x PBS using a pipette, then gently aspirate it.
Fix the spheroids in the 24-well plate by adding 500 µL of fixative solution per well using a 1000 µL pipette.
Allow the fixative to soak the gels for 30 min at room temperature.
Remove the fixative solution using a 1000 µL pipette and discard in a designated waste container.
Rinse the hydrogels by adding 500 µL of 1x PBS to each well.
Aspirate the 1x PBS using a 1000 µL pipette and repeat the rinse with PBS two additional times.
Store the well plate in 500 µL of 1x PBS per well at 4 °C for up to 1 week or use immediately.
Incubate the hydrogel-encapsulated spheroids with primary antibodies for Nestin (200 μg/mL) and SOX2 (200 μg/mL) at a dilution of 1:200 of antibody: PBS.
Aspirate the 1x PBS from the wells using a 1000 µL pipette.
Add 50 µL of the diluted antibody to each well.
Allow staining to be completed for 24 h.
Remove the staining solution using a 1000 µL pipette and discard the waste appropriately.
Aspirate the PBS from each well using a 1000 µL pipette.
Add 500 µL of 1xPBS to each well, which is enough to submerge the hydrogel.
Aspirate the PBS and repeat it two more times.
Store the stained and submerged hydrogel in 1x PBS at 4 °C for up to 2 weeks prior to imaging or image immediately.
Aspirate the 1x PBS from each well using a 1000 µL pipette.
Add 500 µL of 20% (v/v) formamide to each well and allow the hydrogel to incubate for 90 min.
Aspirate the formamide using a 1000 µL pipette and collect the waste in a waste container.
Add 500 µL of 40% (v/v) formamide to the well.
Incubate the hydrogel in the solution for 90 min.
Aspirate the formamide and collect the waste in the waste container.
Add 500 µL of 80% (v/v) formamide to each well.
Incubate the hydrogel in the solution for 90 min.
Aspirate the formamide and dispose in the waste container.
Add 500 µL of 100% (v/v) formamide to each well.
Allow a 24 h incubation prior to imaging.
Properly dispose of formamide waste through laboratory waste management services.
Place the hydrogels in chambered wells with glass coverslip bottoms.
Position the spheroids as close to the coverslip as possible.
Image the samples using a long-working distance objective (10x-20x).
Use Z-stacks for 3D reconstructions.
Quantify the amount of signal present in the optical section relative to the total area of the spheroid for both the cleared and uncleared signal using equation 2.
